title: The ideas that hold biology together
question: What big ideas tie the study of life into one science?
hook: Bacteria, oak trees and people look nothing alike, yet one handful of ideas explains them all.
idea: Biology is unified by a few themes, such as the cell, genes, evolution, energy and homeostasis, and by a history of discoveries that built them.

beats.prompt: match each central theme to what it stands for
beats.explain: These are four of the five fundamental themes at the center of biology.

beats.prompt: put these milestones in the order they happened
items: Schleiden and Schwann promote cell ideas
The Human Genome Project is launched
beats.explain: Linnaeus came in 1735, Schleiden and Schwann in 1838, Mendel in 1865, and the Human Genome Project in 1990.

beats.prompt: sort each organism type into its group
beats.explain: Biologists classify organisms from single-celled archaea and bacteria to multicellular plants, fungi, and animals.

beats.prompt: one step in this account of cell theory is wrong; which?
steps: The basic unit of organisms is the cell.
Individual cells have all the characteristics of life.
All cells arise by spontaneous generation rather than from other cells.
By the 1860s most biologists accepted these tenets as cell theory.
beats.explain: The third tenet is that all cells come from the division of other cells; spontaneous generation is what Schleiden and Schwann wrongly kept supporting.
